caption: Woodcut of ololiuhqui (Rivea corymbosa) from Francisco Hernández's Rerum Medicarum Novae Hispaniae Thesaurus, 1651 edition.
alt: Black-and-white botanical woodcut of a climbing vine with heart-shaped leaves and small buds along the stem, no flowers visible.
credit: Wikimedia Commons, from Francisco Hernández, Rerum Medicarum Novae Hispaniae Thesaurus (Rome, 1651)
note: Contextual image, not a page of Schultes's article: a seventeenth-century botanical woodcut of the morning-glory vine his paper identifies as ololiuqui, not a page of the paper itself.
